question.problem:
The center of the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}-10x=-1$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}-10x & =-1 \\ {x}^{2}-10x-4{y}^{2} & =-1 \\ [{x}^{2}-10x]-4{y}^{2} & =-1 \\ [(x-5)^{2}-25]-4{y}^{2} & =-1 \\ (x-5)^{2}-25-4{y}^{2} & =-1 \\ (x-5)^{2}-4{y}^{2} & =-1+25 \\ (x-5)^{2}-4{y}^{2} & =24 \\ \frac{(x-5)^{2}}{24}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{6} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,5,0\,).$
